devon: kicking off a quant onboarding run for sparrow-lite-int4 canary — seeing weird interleaving in funcall JSON when streaming + kv-cache + batching>1. posting a small raw capture below for context.

devon: ```
--- stream chunk 1 ---
{"output": [{"tool_call": {"name": "search", "arguments": "{\"q\": \"widget\", \"page\": 1}"}, "id": "t-1"}]
--- stream chunk 2 ---
, {"tool_call": {"name": "format", "arguments": "{\"fmt\": \"short\"}"}}]
--- final assembled ---
{"output":[{"tool_call":{"name":"search","arguments":"{\"q\": \"widget\", \"page\": 1}"},"id":"t-1"},{"tool_call":{"name":"format","arguments":"{\"fmt\": \"short\"}"}}]}
```

devon: note how the second chunk starts with a leading comma and closes an array fragment; parser on the host side tries to stitch incremental chunks and sometimes produces an extra delimiter -> parse error. issue spikes only on int4 canary.

sara: is this only when streaming? or also seen in non-streaming batch invokes? :thinking:

devon: only streaming so far. non-streaming (full-response) works fine. suspect interaction of continuous-prefix caching + encoder kernel chunking. parse_fail_rate on canary jumped from 0.4% -> 3.2% after enabling int4 microbatching.

ops-bot: canary-runner: job="sparrow-lite-int4-canary-2026-03-22" parse_fail_rate=0.032 throughput=620req/s mean_lat_ms=87

linh: can you include the tokenized boundary? maybe tokenizer emits a partial escape or multibyte split across frames. also, what's the batch size distribution?

devon: tokenizer snapshot attached — mostly ASCII. batch size was 4 for the failing bucket. here's the per-chunk token idxs we saw: `chunk1 tokens [0..17] chunk2 tokens [18..31]` but the emitted payload adds an extra `,` at chunk boundary sometimes.

mike: hunch: the runtime forwards serialized JSON fragments as-is and downstream stitcher blindly concatenates with a join(',') when reconciling multiple toolcall entries. if a chunk already ends with `]` or `}` the join injects an extra comma. should be idempotent join or use sentinel framing.

ana: small mitigation options: wrap toolcall payloads in NDJSON (one JSON per line) so a streaming parser can read line-by-line, or introduce an explicit sentinel token `<END_TOOL_CALL>` after each toolcall. NDJSON would be minimal server-side change and cheap client-side patch.

ana: also consider temporary mitigation: increase parse-retry budget + backoff so that transient stitch glitches get a quick second chance. but that hides the root cause.

devon: quick experiment: disabled continuous-prefix (flush between tool_call boundaries) for the canary for 2h. parse_fail_rate fell to 0.18% in that window. looks promising.

ops-bot: canary-runner: job="sparrow-lite-int4-canary-2026-03-22-patch" parse_fail_rate=0.0018 throughput=615req/s mean_lat_ms=92

sara: nice! any latency penalty? looks small. we should add a regression test for interleaved-toolcall and add a metric `toolcall_fragmentation_count`.

mike: I'll own a small runtime patch: make the stitcher check for trailing punctuation and avoid double-comma joins; also add NDJSON opt-in header for clients. plan: land as canary patch, monitor parse_fail_rate and tail latency. if stable -> roll to 20% -> 100%. assigning to @mike.

linh: please include the eval harness that reproduces the chunk boundary pattern (I couldn't repro locally). share the micro-batch trace id.

devon: eval-id: eval-2026-03-22-8145. attaching sample generator script (snippet below) — it simulates batching+kv cache+stream chunking with random chunk splits:```python
# pseudo
def make_chunks(json_str, max_chunk_len=40):
    i=0
    out=[]
    while i<len(json_str):
        cut = min(len(json_str), i+ random.randint(10, max_chunk_len))
        out.append(json_str[i:cut])
        i=cut
    return out
```

devon: next steps: mike to PR runtime fix; sara to add metric and regression test; linh to verify tokenizer boundary hypotheses; I'll keep canary patched (flush) until runtime patch is live. target: roll to 20% in 24h if parse_fail_rate < 0.5% and no regression on latency.

ana: sounds good. :thumbsup:

mike: will post PR link shortly and ping this thread. thanks for the capture, devon — saved us a long debug.

devon: thanks everyone — assigning follow-ups in the ticket.
